items.title: Preview seed fixture (rolling)
items.summary: Rolling, fully SYNTHETIC preview-database seed fixture baked from dev@39cc96026f5a (migration head: 20261120120000_add_onboarding_wizard_writer). Preview environments restore fixture.dump.gz (custom-format, gzipped, platform schema only, including _prisma_migrations) BEFORE running a PR's own migrations, so schema changes run against populated tables. RESTORE: apply restore-preamble.sql to the target database first (it creates the platform schema and installs the vector + pg_trgm extensions into it, which pg_dump --schema=platform omits), then run 'gunzip -c fixture.dump.gz | pg_restore -d --no-owner' WITHOUT --exit-on-error (the dump's own CREATE SCHEMA collides benignly with the preamble's). SECURITY INVARIANT: this bake holds no cloud credentials and has no read path to any real database — it runs entirely against a throwaway Postgres container and contains only synthetic rows (Faker-generated, plus the hand-written preview marketplace) and the already-public marketplace agent exports checked into autogpt_platform/backend/agents/. This asset is regenerated on every eligible dev push and weekly; treat it as disposable.

items.summary: ✨ Highlights Connected from the moment you sign in. Continue with Google or Continue with Microsoft now connects your email, files and calendar on the same screen, so Otto can use them from your first chat with no extra setup step. ( #16882 ) More services for Otto. Otto can now connect to Attio and Neon. Skills show each service under its own name and logo, and recognise a service you've already connected instead of asking you to connect it again. ( #16950 , #17265 , #17340 , #17333 , #17347 ) Chats that keep up with you. If your connection drops as you hit Send, Otto now offers Send again instead of losing your message. A message you send while Otto is still finishing its answer gets a reply of its own, in a chat with Otto, in the builder and in Memory. A chat open in another tab shows new replies without a reload, and after you press Stop, your next message goes straight through. ( #17369 , #17249 , #17251 , #16504 , #17365 , #17292 ) 🔒 Security This release fixes several privately reported security issues. We'll publish the advisories once the fixes are live in production. 🧩 Also in this release Otto and AutoPilot Experts pick up where they left off. Hire back an expert you let go, and only the schedules that were running when you let it go start again. Changing an expert's trigger settings now saves, and a schedule that needs a key the expert hasn't been given is refused up front, with a pointer to where you grant it, instead of failing every run. ( #17267 , #17384 , #17380 ) Take the send intent from the app, not the URL ( dd0b5f7 , @Pwuts ) Open the URL the browser host check returned ( 56b80de , @Pwuts ) Task progress clears when Otto empties its task list ( #17118 , @haranishi ) A connect card in an earlier answer no longer offers Proceed ( #17257 , @ntindle ) Send one message when a chat step's sign-ins include an integration server ( #17039 , @kcze ) Otto's new workflows stay off switched-off models ( #17165 , @ntindle ) A free-form model field keeps its value, and a blank one gets the block's default ( #17184 , #17198 , @ntindle ) In a dry-run chat, Otto describes a block instead of simulating it ( #17181 , @ntindle ) Drive files chain between blocks in Otto's runs ( #15118 , @ntindle ) Otto's tools answer sooner by running independent reads side by side ( #15980 , @ntindle ) Model requests are no longer sent twice ( #15446 , @ntindle ) Offer Record again when the transcription API cannot read a recording ( #16505 , @posthog-eu[bot]) Show the backend's reason when an upload is refused with 413 ( #16806 , @posthog-eu[bot]) Library and runs What you type is what runs. A date you pick in the Library reaches your workflow as that day, wherever you are. ( #17315 , #16486 , #17317 , #17212 ) Runs use the key you chose. A workflow runs with the key saved on its step, and a run shows only the key it actually used. items.summary_html:
✨ Highlights
  • Connected from the moment you sign in. Continue with Google or Continue with Microsoft now connects your email, files and calendar on the same screen, so Otto can use them from your first chat with no extra setup step. (#16882)
  • More services for Otto. Otto can now connect to Attio and Neon. Skills show each service under its own name and logo, and recognise a service you've already connected instead of asking you to connect it again. (#16950, #17265, #17340, #17333, #17347)
  • Chats that keep up with you. If your connection drops as you hit Send, Otto now offers Send again instead of losing your message. A message you send while Otto is still finishing its answer gets a reply of its own, in a chat with Otto, in the builder and in Memory. A chat open in another tab shows new replies without a reload, and after you press Stop, your next message goes straight through. (#17369, #17249, #17251, #16504, #17365, #17292)
🔒 Security

This release fixes several privately reported security issues. We'll publish the advisories once the fixes are live in production.

🧩 Also in this release Otto and AutoPilot
  • Experts pick up where they left off. Hire back an expert you let go, and only the schedules that were running when you let it go start again. Changing an expert's trigger settings now saves, and a schedule that needs a key the expert hasn't been given is refused up front, with a pointer to where you grant it, instead of failing every run. (#17267, #17384, #17380)
  • Take the send intent from the app, not the URL (dd0b5f7, @Pwuts)
  • Open the URL the browser host check returned (56b80de, @Pwuts)
  • Task progress clears when Otto empties its task list (#17118, @haranishi)
  • A connect card in an earlier answer no longer offers Proceed (#17257, @ntindle)
  • Send one message when a chat step's sign-ins include an integration server (#17039, @kcze)
  • Otto's new workflows stay off switched-off models (#17165, @ntindle)
  • A free-form model field keeps its value, and a blank one gets the block's default (#17184, #17198, @ntindle)
  • In a dry-run chat, Otto describes a block instead of simulating it (#17181, @ntindle)
  • Drive files chain between blocks in Otto's runs (#15118, @ntindle)
  • Otto's tools answer sooner by running independent reads side by side (#15980, @ntindle)
  • Model requests are no longer sent twice (#15446, @ntindle)
  • Offer Record again when the transcription API cannot read a recording (#16505, @posthog-eu[bot])
  • Show the backend's reason when an upload is refused with 413 (#16806, @posthog-eu[bot])
Library and runs
  • What you type is what runs. A date you pick in the Library reaches your workflow as that day, wherever you are. Very large whole numbers keep every digit, and text that looks like a number, such as "1e5", stays exactly as you typed it. A schedule's next run is labelled with the time zone it's shown in. (#17315, #16486, #17317, #17212)
  • Runs use the key you chose. A workflow runs with the key saved on its step, and a run shows only the key it actually used. A key you set to expire lasts through the end of the day you picked, and once it has expired, a run stops before it starts and tells you to add a new one. (#17362, #17431, #16235)
  • A tidier Library. Move to folder lists your subfolders and always offers My Library, a renamed folder opens under its new name, and the sort menu shows the sort you're on. Deleting a run, template or trigger moves you to what's left, Run now and Rerun task say a run started only once it has, and a template that fails to save keeps what you typed. (#17234, #17235, #17233, #17231, #17209, #17213, #17244, #17219)
  • A stored date that can't be read counts as empty, and clearing a required date disables Start Task again (#17334, @ntindle)
  • Edit workflow opens the active version (#17186, @kcze)
  • The safety popup shows only when its checks are on, and the safe-mode switches are named (#17203, @ntindle)
  • Settings → Integrations shows a key added or deleted in a workflow step's credentials field (#17241, @ntindle)
  • Importing a workflow keeps data keyed "credentials" that isn't a credential (#17224, @ntindle)
  • A running task's duration counts up by the second (#14566, @ntindle)
  • Stopping a run as it starts leaves it stopped, and a stop that arrives while a run is handed to a worker reaches it (#17180, #17193, @ntindle)
  • Sub-graph runs use only the input masks of the run (41035ea, @Pwuts)
  • Moving several workflows to a folder reports the ones it couldn't find and the ones it moved (#16220, @ntindle)
  • Steps stay runnable when an optional credential is deleted (#16194, @ntindle)
  • Match _, % and \ literally in search filters, and refuse NUL (#15661, @ntindle)
  • Output moderation can clear completed steps (#15909, @ntindle)
Builder and workflows
  • Control panel buttons are real, named buttons you can reach with the keyboard (#15847, @ntindle)
  • The builder looks blocks up by id, so a workflow opens faster (#17353, @ntindle)
  • Orchestrator tools get the real type of a nested input (#17187, @kcze)
  • End a stopped Orchestrator's tool loop, and run each graph on its own processor state (ef10f1a, @Pwuts)
  • Route the Orchestrator CLI's model calls through a loopback key relay (1c5aec6, @Pwuts)
Schedules
  • Concurrent schedule creates can't push an account past its limit (#17197, @ntindle)
  • Stopping the scheduler no longer hangs on a job that calls back into it (#17156, @ntindle)
Marketplace
  • Updating your Marketplace listing just works. Publishing a new version of a listed workflow opens its update form, keeps your description and recommended schedule unless you change them, and finds your live listing however many submissions you've made. A rejected older version no longer rolls your live listing back. (#17217, #17221, #17238, #17225, #17239, #16881)
  • Make the workflow name the listing page's h1 (#16912, @ntindle)
  • Deleting a submission that fails answers with a clear error, not a server error (#16492, @ntindle)
  • Organization roles apply to a submission's private media (#17414, @Pwuts)
Integrations and blocks
  • Google Calendar blocks get time zones, declined events and recurrence right (#14910, @ntindle)
  • Gmail Remove Label reports its status, and blank recipients are fixed (#14916, @ntindle)
  • Send Discord File names files after the workspace file and decodes plain data URIs (#17275, @ntindle)
  • Ideogram upscale sends its upload as a list of file parts (#17140, @ntindle)
  • Airtable record calls URL-encode the table name or id (#17323, @harmehak0173)
  • Remove From List returns the item it removed (#17070, @haranishi)
  • The Condition block compares integer strings exactly (#16484, @ntindle)
  • Read RSS Feed no longer stops on entries missing a date, title or link (#15297, @ntindle)
  • The Codex block no longer offers the shut-down gpt-5.1-codex (#17164, @ntindle)
  • Retire models their providers have shut down, or will shut down by 11 Dec (#17103, @ntindle)
  • AI block retries share one deadline (#16172, @ntindle)
  • Time the spend alert on the last HTTP request, not the whole call (#16174, @ntindle)
  • Follow 301/302/303 with a GET, and drop credential headers on cross-origin redirects (#17155, @ntindle)
  • Bound request retries, and resend uploads whole (#17134, @ntindle)
  • Preserve all elements when converting variadic tuples (#14534, @ntindle)
  • Bill AgentMail runs on the platform-managed per-user key (#17063, @0ubbe)
  • Expired ChatGPT credentials can be deleted (#15737, @ntindle)
  • Delete a pasted MCP token without trying to revoke it (#17301, @ntindle)
  • Require an http(s) sign-in URL in the MCP OAuth flow (51e0547, @Pwuts)
  • Reject blank credential secrets and trim padded ones (#15730, @ntindle)
  • Stage each local copy of a file in a folder of its own (#17284, @ntindle)
Billing and account
  • v1 API keys without an organization act in your personal organization (#17415, @Pwuts)
  • A scheduled AutoPilot turn re-checks its organization when it runs (#17416, @Pwuts)
  • A top-up's credits show as soon as you're back from checkout, on the tab you left (#17274, @ntindle)
  • The billing page stops re-reading a failed trial status in a loop (#17279, @ntindle)
  • Charge a spend once when a step after its debit fails (#17121, @ntindle)
  • Bill a step for the model it started on, whatever day it finishes (#17141, @ntindle)
  • Apply Anthropic prompt-tier pricing per request (#16553, @ntindle)
  • Keep the run going when the low-balance check fails (#17061, @0ubbe)
  • Send every password reset link back to the reset page (74ff129, @Pwuts)
  • Onboarding keeps saving after one of its own saves was lost (#17160, @ntindle)
  • The personal organization, its badge and avatars show correctly (#17153, @ntindle)
  • Refuse invitations into personal organizations (#16625, @ntindle)
  • End session checks that never get an answer (#17024, @ntindle)
  • Notification preferences load for a stored reserved-domain email (#14992, @ntindle)
Pages, sharing and reliability
  • A page that doesn't exist shows "not found" instead of crashing the app (#17283, @ntindle)
  • Shared chats and runs say "not found" only when the link is gone, and offer a retry otherwise (#17214, #17208, @ntindle)
  • Times like "5 minutes ago" read the same on the server and in your browser (#17331, @ntindle)
  • A request is retried once when its connection was dropped on the way (#17361, @ntindle)
  • Send the WebSocket sign-in token in the first message instead of the URL (#17288, @kcze)
  • Retry a WebSocket subscribe that fails with a retryable error (#17056, @ntindle)
  • Keep shared-cache Redis reads off the event loop (#17074, @ntindle)
  • Return a generic detail for 5xx errors (#15662, @ntindle)
  • Stop sending handled network failures to Sentry (#16441, @posthog-eu[bot])
  • Log the WebSocket error event at debug, not as an error (#16615, @posthog-eu[bot])
  • Report 401s between our own services to Sentry (#17062, @0ubbe)
  • Rotate an anonymous id an older account already merged (#16837, @posthog-eu[bot])
  • Admin failed-execution diagnostics go by when a run ended (#15823, @ntindle)
Local PC
  • Connect a second computer from the Local PC folder dialog (#16906, @ntindle)
  • Local PC executor follow-ups from review (#16890, @ntindle)
Mobile app
  • The app signs in existing accounts, and an account with no active plan is asked to get one (#17072, #17146, @0ubbe)
  • Hire an expert opens with your team and lists jobs by area (#17057, @0ubbe)
  • Expert pages follow the web's, with a new Files page and a tidier files panel (#17319, @0ubbe)
  • Tables in chat scroll sideways (#17402, @0ubbe)
  • Crash reporting, over-the-air updates, and a minimum app version the server can require through the optional MOBILE_MIN_APP_VERSION (#17400, @0ubbe)
🛠️ For self-hosters and developers
  • Readiness check. The new /health/ready checks the database, and a failed health check answers 503 (#16501, @ntindle).
  • Idle connections stay open longer than the proxies in front of them. The backend's new SERVER_KEEP_ALIVE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS defaults to 620, and the Compose frontend and the single-container image's nginx now keep idle connections for 620 seconds, up from 65 (#17338, #17345, @ntindle).
  • Admins behind your own proxy. An admin behind a proxy that ends TLS, or on plain http, is no longer sent from the admin pages to Home (#17350, #17332, @ntindle).
  • Run outputs hold what an Agent Output block produced, in the External API too: for a block with a format set, that's the formatted text rather than the raw value (#15908, @ntindle).
  • External API. A workflow looked up without a version returns its active version (#15664, @ntindle), and the v1 results endpoint returns outputs that aren't text instead of failing (#17093, @ntindle).
  • Faster start. The backend's boot-time model pass runs four statements instead of hundreds, so API servers start serving sooner (#17144, @ntindle).
  • Notification service. With APP_ENV=prod and BEHAVE_AS=cloud it refuses to start without POSTMARK_SERVER_API_TOKEN. The shipped setups set neither, so they're unaffected (#14409, @ntindle).
  • Compose mounts the workspace volume on every service that reads, writes or erases it (#17312, @ntindle), and RabbitMQ's healthcheck no longer writes the broker's Erlang cookie (#17248, @ntindle).
  • Skills catalog. It downloads without GitHub's API when no token is set, and retries through a GitHub blip (#17354, #17351, @ntindle).
  • Images pick up Debian's package updates as soon as they're published (#17352, @ntindle).
  • Require a session id on every user token (#16857, @ntindle)
  • The input renderer's modules load in any order (#17289, #17297, @ntindle)
  • The Local PC companion's source now lives in this repository, under local_executor/ (#16575, @ntindle)
  • The mobile app builds as one app, against dev or production (#17148, #17320, @0ubbe)

Dependencies: 10 bumps (#16940, #16939, #15513, #15897, #17082, #17083, #17084, #16802, #17080, #16656).

CI, tests and developer tooling: 38 changes (#17379, #17368, #17290, #17337, #17346, #17324, #17314, #17311, #17131, #17291, #17300, #17299, #17296, #17287, #17271, #17273, #17266, #17258, #17254, #17246, #17226, #17222, #17216, #17211, #17210, #17205, #17206, #17202, #17199, #17196, #17195, #17194, #17191, #17157, #17152, #16626, #15453, #15144).

Documentation: 1 change (#15179).

items.title: I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the AI
items.summary: A few years ago talking heads and AM radio personalities went cookoo over AI. The warnings were replete with assertations of total destruction. I blew them off as doomsdayesque viewer/listener headline/listener bastards that saw dollar signs in words. Assuredly, they completely misunderstood the technology and the intricacies of how AI functions and what it was capable of. They read enough science fiction to regurgitate what sounded like knowledge of the future. Interestingly, they were largely right in the end. The tech has evolved fantastically quick. The wildest scenarios preposed from previous predicions is becoming realistic. I do not worry about those scenarios. I do not fear the wildest predictions. Throughout history humans have developed weapons, ideas, technologies, and systems that detractors predicted would kill us all or would lead to insurmountable changes to society. Electricity is not the devil. The printing press was not a detriment to society. AI will fundamentally change many things. That is a good thing. Humanity will forever be preserved. What is Humanity? We will perpetually find out. Happy Thanksgiving to everyone.

items.title: Show HN: Talira – Search engine for software, built for AI agents
items.summary: Hi HN, I'm Nathan. I wanted to share a project that I've been working on this month. A few weeks ago, my Rust target folders had grown to about 70 GB across many git worktrees, and I asked Claude to figure out how to stop that from happening. It couldn't find much online, so we started to build our own workaround using some unstable cargo flags. Then someone on r/rust asked why we hadn't just used kache. Someone else mentioned Mr Boxington on a GitHub issue (another great solution). I also got annoyed that my Claude Code sessions would constantly ask me to reauthenticate my MCP servers, which happens when you run a lot of them in parallel. An agent couldn't find any good "MCP proxy" so we started planning and building our own. I searched Google myself and found MCPProxy.app. It worked pretty well so I wrote a blog post and shared it on X. Some people replied and told me that Executor.sh was an even better solution. They were right, so I switched to Executor. After all this, I decided to build Talira: A search engine for software that an AI agent can check before it starts building your own solution. You describe the problem in plain words ("my Rust target folders use 80 GB across git worktrees"). Talira searches the catalog using vector embeddings and uses Jev for filtering and reranking. To try it: - Search on https://talira.ai - Add the MCP server to Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user talira https://mcp.talira.ai/mcp Your agent can also send a report after each search: the problem in general terms, what you tried, what you kept and why. The idea is that it can eventually become a crowd-sourced database of tools that people actually chose and continued using over time. It's currently in beta and the catalog still has a lot of gaps. I should also mention that I'm aware that ChatGPT and Claude already know a lot and are already very good at search. So there are plenty of cases where you don't need Talira at all. I'll need to collect some more real-world searches before I can benchmark it properly to see if it makes any difference. I'd like to know if you've ever had any similar experiences. Let me know if an AI wasn't able to find a good solution that already existed. Thanks for reading!
items.summary_html:
Hi HN, I'm Nathan. I wanted to share a project that I've been working on this month.

A few weeks ago, my Rust target folders had grown to about 70 GB across many git worktrees, and I asked Claude to figure out how to stop that from happening. It couldn't find much online, so we started to build our own workaround using some unstable cargo flags. Then someone on r/rust asked why we hadn't just used kache. Someone else mentioned Mr Boxington on a GitHub issue (another great solution).

I also got annoyed that my Claude Code sessions would constantly ask me to reauthenticate my MCP servers, which happens when you run a lot of them in parallel. An agent couldn't find any good "MCP proxy" so we started planning and building our own. I searched Google myself and found MCPProxy.app. It worked pretty well so I wrote a blog post and shared it on X. Some people replied and told me that Executor.sh was an even better solution. They were right, so I switched to Executor.

After all this, I decided to build Talira: A search engine for software that an AI agent can check before it starts building your own solution. You describe the problem in plain words ("my Rust target folders use 80 GB across git worktrees"). Talira searches the catalog using vector embeddings and uses Jev for filtering and reranking.

To try it:

- Search on https://talira.ai

- Add the MCP server to Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user talira https://mcp.talira.ai/mcp

Your agent can also send a report after each search: the problem in general terms, what you tried, what you kept and why. The idea is that it can eventually become a crowd-sourced database of tools that people actually chose and continued using over time.

It's currently in beta and the catalog still has a lot of gaps. I should also mention that I'm aware that ChatGPT and Claude already know a lot and are already very good at search. So there are plenty of cases where you don't need Talira at all. I'll need to collect some more real-world searches before I can benchmark it properly to see if it makes any difference.

I'd like to know if you've ever had any similar experiences. Let me know if an AI wasn't able to find a good solution that already existed.

Thanks for reading!
